findings.expected: '${OTHER}': the flat grammar ends the word at the first closing brace, so the word is the literal '${OTHER' and the trailing '}' stays literal; a brace-balanced recursive repair instead returns 'expanded', yet every grader case still passes and grader.py prints 'ok'.
findings.gap: The grader never exercises a nested ${...} inside the alternate word, so it accepts a repair that violates the flat/nonrecursive requirement. The 'literal' case only asserts A=${BASE:+$OTHER} -> '$OTHER' (bare-$ literal, already satisfied by a first-close match plus a literal word), B=${BASE:+} -> '', C=x${BASE:+α}${BASE:+β}y -> 'xαβy' (adjacent whole substitutions), and D=${BASE:+unfinished -> literal. No case feeds a word containing a balanced inner ${NAME}.
findings.wrong_repair: Match the expression with brace balancing (e.g., count braces so ${BASE:+${OTHER}} is captured as one match, word = '${OTHER}') and recursively resolve the captured word via parse_variables().resolve(env) before substitution.

answer.limitations: Reviewed only flat, nonrecursive interpolation and literal alternate words, as instructed; precedence, legacy, and disabled-path behavior were not reviewed. The packet omitted grader.py bytes 2048-2365, so I read them via the frozen-source tool to confirm no nested-word assertion exists there. Only one counterexample is provided, and the repair was not implemented.
